I.NEG1.obstruction: Prime-phase constructions meant to keep f(n+h1)f(n+h2) biased while f stays uniformly non-pretentious met 'dense compatibility constraints' (L45). The phases at the primes dividing n and n+h would have to be coordinated for a positive proportion of n, and that over-constrains f(p) across overlapping sets of primes.
I.NEG1.lesson_statement: There is no cheap prime-phase counterexample, so commit to a proof (C1).
I.NEG1.generality: local (a sketch only; ~20 words of summary)
I.NEG1.known_in_literature: Consistent with the literature. The only known way the ORIGINAL Elliott conjecture fails is a function imitating different twists n^{it} at different scales (Matomaki-Radziwill-Tao 2015, Appendix B), and the uniform hypothesis in the prompt excludes exactly that. The corrected conjecture is believed true; Tao 2016 proves its log-averaged form.
I.NEG1.influence: enabling: motivates the switch to proof proposals (L46)
I.NEG1.what_was_not_learned: The summary does not show the model connecting the failed construction to the MRT scale-varying-twist mechanism, i.e. it does not say WHY uniform non-pretentiousness kills the natural counterexamples.

I.a1.obstruction: A dilation graph joins n and n+hd only when d | n, a sparse condition. Removing (centering) that condition costs either reciprocal mass (comparable-size primes, I.a1.1) or scale (wide dilations, I.a1.2). Tao's entropy decrement avoids the dilemma only at an unspecified scale (I.a1.3).
I.a1.lesson_statement: The central difficulty is removing sparse divisibility conditions without changing the scale (C3a). Any graph must have both large reciprocal mass and scale localization.
I.a1.generality: general (it states the problem's core trade-off for every graph approach)
I.a1.known_in_literature: Known: this is the ordinary-vs-logarithmic averaging gap. Log averages are dilation invariant (Tao 2016, Forum Math Pi), ordinary averages are not. Helfgott-Radziwill 2021 and Pilatte 2023/26 work only with logarithmic weights for this reason.
I.a1.salvage: The graph framework itself is kept and resumed at I.a4 (L65).
I.a1.influence: decisive: I.a4 meets both requirements, with weights A^{omega(d)} for mass and narrow multiplicative intervals for scale

I.a1.1.obstruction: Primes in one dyadic-type range [P, 2P] have reciprocal mass sum 1/p ~ 1/log P, which is far too small to drive graph expansion or a spectral saving.
I.a1.1.lesson_statement: One range of comparable primes has too little reciprocal mass, so the mass must be amplified, by many ranges or weighted products (C2).
I.a1.1.known_in_literature: Known: the reciprocal-mass budget is the basic constraint in Helfgott-Radziwill (arXiv:2103.06853). Pilatte's composite labels (products of primes from several ranges) exist to amplify it.
I.a1.1.influence: decisive: weights A^{omega(d)} giving the broad degree (1+A)^{omega_S(n)} (I.a4.1). Part II analogue: J supplies of mass ~W each, total W^J (II.b1.7; cross-part reuse inferred).

I.a1.2.obstruction: Dilations n -> dn by d of very different sizes compare averages at different scales X and X/d. An ordinary average at the terminal scale cannot absorb that comparison; a logarithmic average can.
I.a1.2.lesson_statement: Steps must be localized to a narrow multiplicative window, so all dilations in one comparison have essentially the same size (C3).
I.a1.2.generality: general (rules out naive transfers of log-averaged graph arguments to ordinary averages)
I.a1.2.known_in_literature: Known: this is the reason Tao 2016 and HR/Pilatte are logarithmic. The paper's intro says logarithmic weighting 'combines information from many multiplicative scales'.
I.a1.2.influence: decisive: narrow intervals near a scale H (I.a4.3, I.a4.5); paper's 'short multiplicative intervals' (H<d<=tau H) in both parts

I.a1.3.obstruction: Entropy decrement finds SOME scale where the independence estimate holds (pigeonhole over scales). It cannot be forced to hold at the given terminal scale, so it yields log-averaged or almost-all-scales results only.
I.a1.3.lesson_statement: Entropy-decrement methods choose an unspecified scale and cannot give every-scale ordinary cancellation (C4).
I.a1.3.generality: general (rules out the Tao/Tao-Teravainen family as a direct route)
I.a1.3.known_in_literature: Known: Tao 2016 (log averages), Tao-Teravainen 2019 (exceptional scales of log density 0), KMT 2023 (full upper log density).
I.a1.3.influence: contributory: relearned at I.a4.9; the final fixed-B-then-X->infinity order of limits (I.a4.18) controls one prescribed scale B, which is the opposite design (inferred)

I.a2.obstruction: Every operator-algebraic or adelic-dynamical tool tried either needs a property equivalent to the target cancellation (tracial/KMS), needs an extra assumption (normality), fails for infinite invariant measure, or does not cover the singular kernels that arise.
I.a2.lesson_statement: Dilation-invariant adelic reformulations bring no scale-uniform mechanism; the needed regularity is as hard as the conjecture (C5x).
I.a2.generality: general (rules out a whole transfer family: Bost-Connes / Toeplitz-algebra equilibrium theory)
I.a2.known_in_literature: Not a stated result in the literature. The link between Chowla-type statements and dynamics on adeles/Furstenberg systems is known (Frantzikinakis-Host, Tao's Furstenberg-correspondence work), but this specific KMS route is not a known approach to Elliott.
I.a2.what_was_not_learned: Not stated: whether the model saw that dilation-invariant (logarithmic) structure is exactly what ordinary averages lack (C3). The adelic detour repeats that clause in another language.

I.a2.1.obstruction: Smoothing in the real scale looked promising, but restoring the finite-adelic (congruence) coordinate prevented inferring the continuity the argument needed.
I.a2.1.lesson_statement: Archimedean smoothing does not pass to the congruence coordinate (C5).
I.a2.1.known_in_literature: Not a stated known result; plausible (congruence information is totally disconnected)

I.a2.2.obstruction: The classification of equilibrium states on the Toeplitz algebra of the affine semigroup over N would identify the kernel only if it had a tracial property, and that property is 'closely related to the desired cancellation'.
I.a2.2.lesson_statement: Using the KMS classification presupposes a property equivalent to the conclusion (C6).
I.a2.2.known_in_literature: Not known as a stated barrier; it is the model's own observation

I.a2.3.obstruction: Ergodicity gives a dilation-invariant formulation, but the invariant measure is infinite, so the simple invariant-probability argument fails. Normality of the limiting state remains an extra assumption.
I.a2.3.lesson_statement: Ergodicity with infinite measure plus an unproved normality assumption does not give cancellation (C7).
I.a2.3.known_in_literature: The ergodicity result is known (Neshveyev 2002); its inapplicability here is the model's observation

I.a2.4.obstruction: Mixing results for finite von Neumann algebras concern normal states and maps. The kernels the argument needs are singular, so they are not classified.
I.a2.4.lesson_statement: Normal-state mixing theory does not reach singular kernels (C8).
I.a2.4.known_in_literature: Known scope limitation of Cameron-Fang-Mukherjee 2013 (normal setting)

I.a2.5.obstruction: TT's quantitative theorem allows shifts and moduli only up to a polylogarithmic range (and keeps an exceptional set of scales). The proposed dilation window needs larger shifts and moduli.
I.a2.5.lesson_statement: TT26 cannot be plugged in: its shift/modulus range is too short (C9).
I.a2.5.known_in_literature: Known: TT26 (arXiv:2512.01739) Theorem 3.1 / Remark 3.2 allow slowly growing coefficients outside an exceptional set of scales.
I.a2.5.influence: contributory: relearned explicitly at I.a4.9 (L112-113) and rechecked at II.b1.12 (L196-198)

I.a3.obstruction: A polynomial substitution n = P(m) that preserves lambda-signs maps onto a density-zero set, so cancellation along it says nothing about the full average.
I.a3.lesson_statement: Sign-preserving polynomial substitutions have sparse images; a positive-density argument is still needed (C10).
I.a3.known_in_literature: Known in substance: Helfgott's thesis (2003) handles parity of homogeneous binary forms, a different (sparse, two-variable) problem

I.a4.5.1.obstruction: Bounding a return-edge factor pointwise and removing it BEFORE the signed integration over prime residues destroys cancellation needed elsewhere in the walk.
I.a4.5.1.lesson_statement: Take signed averages before absolute values: keep return factors inside the primewise integration (C12).
I.a4.5.1.generality: general (a principle for every high-trace computation with centered factors)
I.a4.5.1.known_in_literature: Known as a principle: HR21 and Pilatte integrate singleton primes first. Pilatte's sieve-inside-trace estimates have the same order of operations.
I.a4.5.1.influence: decisive: reused at I.a4.16 (singleton cancellation under conditioning) and in the paper's 'signed averages are taken before absolute values'. Probable cross-part echo in Part II's 'Exact centering before absolute values' (q:mixed-difference).

I.a4.5.obstruction: Normalizing prime-product weights by vertex degrees changed the centering needed to cancel primes that appear on only one trace edge. Repeated vertices, disconnected prime occurrences and branching paths complicated the per-step saving. A verbatim note demands that singleton residues stay approximately independent and uniform under conditioning.
I.a4.5.lesson_statement: The centering constant must be matched to the vertex normalization, and singleton cancellation must survive conditioning (C13).
I.a4.5.verbatim_excerpt: Singleton cancellation requires n residue for singleton primes approximate independent uniform when no Y failure, even conditioned on repeated prime hits etc. Need upper bound for deviation.
I.a4.5.known_in_literature: Partly known: cancellation at singleton primes is the engine of HR21 and Pilatte. Matching a NON-mean-zero centering theta/p to the endpoint normalization is not, to my knowledge, in those papers (the paper presents it as its own device).
I.a4.5.salvage: Narrow-interval composite steps, fresh-prime savings and divisor-count cutoffs all survive into the final graph

I.a4.8.1.obstruction: MRT's corrected non-pretentiousness condition requires the MINIMUM pretentious distance over characters of bounded modulus and twists |t|<=X to diverge for every fixed modulus bound. Excluding each fixed twist separately is too weak.
I.a4.8.1.lesson_statement: Uniformity in t over |t|<=X is essential, which is the prompt's hypothesis (C15).
I.a4.8.1.generality: general (it is the conceptual content of 'corrected' Elliott)
I.a4.8.1.known_in_literature: Known: Matomaki-Radziwill-Tao 2015 (corrected arXiv v3, 2022), Section 1.1 and Appendix B. KMT 2023 shows what the weaker pointwise hypothesis still gives (full upper log density of scales only).
I.a4.8.1.influence: decisive: I.a4.18 checks that finite-prime cutoff twists preserve the uniform hypothesis; paper lem:finite-prime-stability

I.a4.11.obstruction: No failure is stated. Several layered core bands were replaced by one narrow upper band, which is presented as a simplification.
I.a4.11.lesson_statement: One narrow core band suffices; layering is unnecessary (C16).
I.a4.11.known_in_literature: n/a (design choice). The final paper has the single core band C = {B^{1-eta} < log p <= B}.
I.a4.11.influence: decisive for the final band structure (paper eq:prime-bands)
I.a4.11.what_was_not_learned: The summary never describes the layered design, so what it was meant to buy is unknown.

I.a4.18.1.obstruction: No reason is stated. The upper-bound sieve appeal was replaced by truncated inclusion-exclusion estimates for one and two rough integers.
I.a4.18.1.lesson_statement: Use explicit truncated inclusion-exclusion (with counting errors) for one and two rough integers instead of a black-box upper-bound sieve (C17).
I.a4.18.1.known_in_literature: Known technique (even-order Bonferroni truncation, Brun). Paper lem:rough-multiplier: 'even inclusion-exclusion gives 1_{r(n)=0} <= sum_{j<=s} (-1)^j binom(r,j)'.
I.a4.18.1.what_was_not_learned: Likely motivation (analyst's inference): uniformity in the rough modulus and explicit counting errors for PAIRS (n, n+h).

II.b1.1.obstruction: The prime supplies grow with X, so the product of all moduli (the joint CRT period) can exceed the length of the integer interval. Averaging over the full joint period then gives no useful finite-scale estimate ('Finite CRT prevents mixing over P for cutoffs').
II.b1.1.lesson_statement: Independent-residue calculations cannot be transferred to finite intervals by exact CRT. A pseudo-randomness transfer that only needs low-order independence is required (C18).
II.b1.1.verbatim_excerpt: Need exact cancellation singleton and nonnegative support of low-rank. Finite CRT prevents mixing over P for cutoffs.
II.b1.1.generality: general (every argument with growing prime supplies at a fixed finite scale)
II.b1.1.known_in_literature: Known phenomenon: the sieve 'fundamental lemma' / Brun truncation exists because only low-order independence of residues holds in short ranges. Linial-Nisan 1990 (approximate inclusion-exclusion) links it to bounded independence; the paper cites them, the trace does not.
II.b1.1.salvage: Independent residue model kept as auxiliary law (paper 'The independent residue space')

II.b1.3a.obstruction: Witnesses obtained one singleton label at a time (pairwise changes) need not be jointly present in one residue configuration, so they cannot be combined into simultaneous constraints.
II.b1.3a.lesson_statement: Use the full mixed difference over all singleton coordinates: a nonzero mixed difference forces one hybrid where witnesses cover ALL singleton labels at once (C19).
II.b1.3a.verbatim_excerpt: Mixed difference property stronger than pairwise changes
II.b1.3a.generality: local (but it is the key move of Part II)
II.b1.3a.known_in_literature: Nearest known: Pilatte 2026 Lemmas 11.6, 13.1, 13.6 (active primes, triangular constraints, witnesses). The mixed-difference/hybrid existence argument is not attributed in the paper.
